chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade unsheathing the sword in the mosque, and sharpening the arrows in the mosque. He said: 'It was built for other than that.'

key_terms.لِغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ: For other than that (i.e., for worship)

ai.seo_question: What martial activities are forbidden inside the mosque according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the principle of 'khushu' (reverence) by prohibiting martial preparations like unsheathing swords and sharpening arrows, actions that signify readiness for combat rather than devotion. Scholars emphasize that these prohibitions preserve the mosque's sanctity as a space for spiritual tranquility, distinct from the bustle of military activity. The Imam’s clarification that the mosque is 'built for other than that' underscores its primary purpose as a house of worship and remembrance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from unsheathing the sword in the Masjid, and from sharpening the arrows in the Masjid’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, it has been built for other than that’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
The Messenger of Allah prohibited unsheathing of swords and trimming arrows in the Masjid saying, “Masjid is built for something other than such things.’””
